title: Queue depth telemetry sleuthing - notes
content:
Quick summary:
- Incident: repeated throughput regressions on demo-hosted cluster (eu-west-1) starting ~2024-11-02 09:18 UTC. Visible as 20–40% drop in tokens/sec for the text-gen route with no config change announced.
- Primary suspicion: continuous-batcher queue depth / drain misconfiguration interacting with a shift in request token distribution (more short requests, more cold starts).
- This doc is a scratchpad of commands tried, logs captured, hypotheses, quick experiments, and next steps. Purpose: breadcrumbs for follow-ups and for writing a small postmortem once resolved.

Observed symptoms & quick metrics snapshot (09:18–09:45 UTC):
- tokens/sec (route /v1/generate): baseline ~1.2M tokens/s -> dropped to ~0.75M for 20 min windows.
- p50 latency: 28ms -> 42ms; p95: 190ms -> 280ms (spiky).
- avg batch_size reported by continuous-batcher: 46 -> 11 (big drop).
- continuous-batcher.queue_depth (custom metric): 120 -> spike to 420 then slow drain.
- kv_cache.hit_rate: no major change (~87% -> 84%).
- worker_cpu% and GPU util%: GPU util dropped 20% (more idle), CPU per-request increased slightly.

Immediate context / what changed around that time:
- No infra deploys in that window (checked release-engineering release calendar).
- Model versions pinned; no rollout.
- Traffic profile: slight increase in short-chat (avg tokens/request down from 300 to 40) — could be client-side change. Confirmed a few product teams ramping up a new demo.

Commands & queries used while investigating:
- scrape metrics from prometheus for the period:
  curl -sS "http://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=continuous_batcher_avg_batch_size&start=1698927480&end=1698928380&step=15" | jq '.'
- pod-level logs (example):
  kubectl -n inference logs deploy/continuous-batcher --since=40m | grep -i "batch_size" | tail -n 200
- check batcher flags for running replica:
  kubectl -n inference exec -it <batcher-pod> -- ps aux | grep continuous-batcher
  kubectl -n inference exec -it <batcher-pod> -- curl -s localhost:9000/debug/flags
- inspect trace for a slow request (trace id from tracing UI):
  span details show wait_for_batch_time per request increased 3–8ms -> now 14–40ms for many requests.
- spot-checking queue state via admin endpoint:
  curl -sS "http://batcher-admin:8001/queues" | jq '. | map({name:.name, depth:.depth, head_age_ms:.head_age_ms})'

Representative log snippets (anonymized):
- WARNING continuous_batcher: queue_depth=398 head_age_ms=4100 drains=0
- INFO batcher: created batch size=8 tokens_est=290 throughput_est=12.3k/s
- DEBUG scheduling: attempted fill=64 but got=9 (timeout limit reached)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Client traffic distribution changed (many short requests) -> fewer opportunities for large batches. Batcher times out earlier and emits small batches frequently; continuous-batcher expected long tail of medium-length requests to reach threshold.
2) Batcher timeout/latency configuration too aggressive for new distribution (window_ms set to 5ms, max_batch_fill_time_ms set to 6ms). With short requests arriving bursty, worker sees many tiny batches and GPU utilization drops.
3) Queue depth metric spike suggests backlog: either consumer (batcher->worker) throughput dipped due to GC pauses or slow startup of worker threads (e.g., Python worker process).
4) Token accounting bug: under some request shapes (many function calls / metadata), tokens_est incorrectly low, causing batch fill heuristics to think batch size is reached earlier.
5) Cross-talk with prefetching/KV cache: prefetch requests push many tiny items into queue (not full requests) causing queue depth to look high while real batching opportunities are fewer.

Experiments & what I changed (chronological):
- 09:35: increased continuous-batcher.window_ms from 5 -> 15 (temp via admin endpoint). Rationale: allow more time to accumulate requests.
  Result: avg batch_size moved from 11 -> 22 over ~6 minutes, tokens/sec recovered ~8% but p95 latency increased slightly (as expected for waiting window).
- 09:52: rolled back window_ms to 5 to test alternate theory. Throughput stayed slightly improved (11->15 avg batch) — suggests there might be momentum or another factor.
- 10:05: forced GC on a suspect worker (hotfix) and restarted one worker pod that had frequent minor OOM events in last week.
  Result: minimal immediate effect.
- 10:24: toggled a feature-flag to disable prefetching of embeddings on the demo route (this reduces background tiny-requests).
  Result: queue_depth spike frequency decreased; batch_size stabilized around ~30, tokens/sec improved ~18% vs incident trough.

What the logs told us after toggling prefetch:
- queue entries decreased that were <50 bytes (these looked like prefetch probes).
- measured batcher wait_for_batch_time decreased slightly, but more importantly batches were fuller.

Correlated artifacts / clues: 
- Traffic telemetry (product team A) shows a client-side SDK version change at 09:10 that enabled lazy prefetch. This corresponds with demo spike.
- Slack thread #serving-runtime had a ping from Solutions at 09:22 describing slower demo performance — same customers.
- No kube node evictions or autoscaler events in the same window.

Preliminary conclusions (working):
- Primary driver appears to be client-side behavior change (more short/prefetch-ish requests) which exposed an overly aggressive batching timeout + a noisy prefetch pattern that inserted lots of tiny queue entries. These combined to reduce effective batch density, causing lower GPU utilization and throughput regression.
- There may be secondary contributors: minor worker instability (OOMs) reducing consumer drain rate occasionally; and a potential token_estimation edge-case that makes some requests artificially 'light' for the batcher. Need to validate token accounting.

Action items / TODO (short-term):
- (OPS) Roll a conservative config: window_ms = 12, max_batch_size = 64, min_batch_emit = 8 across demo clusters for 24h (seek config owner approval).
- (ENG) Add a metric for "tiny-queue-entry-rate" (size < 128 bytes) to detect prefetch noise in future.
- (ENG) Add histograms of token_est per request and token_est vs actual_token_count to catch token accounting mismatches.
- (SRE) Instrument consumer drain rate (items/sec) per worker to spot consumer slowdowns faster.
- (PRODUCT) Contact product team A to revert/adjust lazy prefetch SDK behavior or to throttle prefetch in client.
- (DEV) Create a unit test that simulates mixed traffic (50% short prefetch probes, 50% normal) and validate batching heuristics hold.

Longer-term thoughts (notes to self):
- Consider multi-class queues: isolate prefetch/probe requests in a separate low-priority queue so they don't interfere with main batching.
- Batcher could weight entries by "effective token density" rather than count; prefer to accumulate high-token-weight requests first.
- Add dynamic window_ms that adapts to observed short/long request ratios.

Open questions / what to verify next:
- Is token_est computed strictly from tokenizer? Are there shapes (function-calls, metadata) that cause it to undercount? Add sampling to verify.
- Was any autoscaling or affinity change in infra that could cause intermittent reduced consumer throughput? (No evidence now, but keep checking node-level metrics for CPU steal).
- Are there other clients enabling the same SDK change in other regions? Check traffic across eu-west-1 and us-west-2.

Notes for postmortem draft (if confirmed):
- Root cause likely combination of product change (lazy prefetch) + batching timeout config mismatch. Contributing: lack of tiny-entry telemetry and missing consumer-drain metrics.
- Remediations: telemetry, config tweaks, SDK guidance, maybe queue-class isolation.

Reference links & breadcrumbs:
- Jira ENGINF-4273 (investigation)
- GH PR 1839 (batcher admin endpoint change used during testing)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime, message ts 1698927350 (pings from Solutions about demo slow)

Quick TODO checklist for me: 
- [ ] Open a tiny telemetry spike dashboard (tiny-entry-rate).
- [ ] Push config change to staging and run 2h load test with mixed traffic generator.
- [ ] Follow up with product A to request rolling back lazy prefetch in demo until we ship queue isolation.
- [ ] Draft brief incident note for the team summarizing timeline + immediate mitigations.

Random notes / stray ideas:
- Could add a "drop small prefetches when queue_depth > X" fallback to protect main traffic.
- When window_ms > 10 we saw improved tokens/sec but customer-experience might be worse for very low-latency clients — consider route-specific overrides.

End of scratchpad. Update this doc with test results and final PM/incident notes once we converge.
